extracted.intended_audience: readers interested in technology, media industry, and news product design
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and evaluating news-app homepages and recommendation systems that balance personalization, political diversity, user interface, sourcing, emergency information, and monetization strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personalized but politically balanced range of stories
rubrics_metrics.description: SmartNews promises to "serve its readers a personalized, but politically balanced range of stories."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance personalization with exposure to multiple viewpoints to avoid filter bubbles; prioritize both relevance to the user and political diversity in recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit partisan labeling and toggling (News From All Sides)
rubrics_metrics.description: "News From All Sides... marks the partisan spectrum of news stories clearly, and allows readers to toggle between them."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make partisan orientation transparent (examples: mapping outlets to left/center/right) and let users navigate across the spectrum; use labeling as a tool for transparency rather than claiming it fully solves bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithmic priorities: political balancing and diversification
rubrics_metrics.description: SmartNews "began ranking what they called 'political balancing' and 'diversification' as priorities in their algorithms."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly encode diversity and balance objectives in ranking signals so algorithms surface multiple political viewpoints rather than only maximizing engagement-based homogeneity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human curation to enforce standards
rubrics_metrics.description: A "team of human curators backs up the software, keeping an eye on curation standards by flagging things like inappropriate images."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine automated ranking with human oversight to monitor quality, flag problematic content (e.g., inappropriate imagery), and correct algorithmic errors or edge cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curated homepages mixing local and national sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Within each category is "a curated homepage of stories, drawn from both local and national news sources."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design category homepages to blend local and national coverage to serve both community-relevant and broader-context stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simple, streamlined user interface and clear category tabs
rubrics_metrics.description: Hamamoto overhauled the UI: he "pared them back, bringing in a streamlined interface and a sans serif font" with "a handful of article categories" at the top.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer uncluttered layouts, clear category affordances (e.g., color-coded tabs), and readable typography to improve discoverability and usability compared to cluttered designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency and public-health information hubs
rubrics_metrics.description: SmartNews added "high-traffic public emergency and natural disaster updates," "Covid-19 information hubs," and tracking portals for hurricanes, wildfires, and typhoons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include dedicated, high-visibility hubs and dashboards for crises and public-health information (alerts, eligibility notifications, maps) to serve public-interest needs during emergencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sourcing and data completeness via liaison and manual scraping
rubrics_metrics.description: To fill databases, a SmartNews team "liaised with government agencies, manually scraping data from government documents that weren’t fully digitized."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When official data is fragmented or not machine-friendly, proactively liaise with agencies and use manual data collection to ensure accurate, up-to-date public-service information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monetization: advertising placement and revenue strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: "Advertising is SmartNews’ main source of revenue across the versions, and inline and video ads appear at the top of category pages."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place ads (inline/video) strategically in category pages while balancing user experience; consider ad-driven incentive programs with publishers as part of the revenue model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publisher partnerships and incentive programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Growth efforts included an "incentive program that pays national publications to bring their articles onto the platform" and "audience-development partnerships with national publications."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use paid partnerships and content deals to onboard publishers, increase content breadth, and drive referral traffic; balance incentives with editorial standards and platform neutrality goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: User research, localization, and product-market fit testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Hamamoto tested the prototype with English-teaching cafes (eikaiwa), then did "more rigorous user testing in San Francisco and New York," and localized UI changes for international markets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct inexpensive, local user research early and iterative testing in target markets; adapt UI, taxonomy (tabs), and features to local expectations and behavior patterns (e.g., commuter habits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Growth and evaluation metrics (MAUs, referral traffic, pageviews)
rubrics_metrics.description: The article cites metrics such as monthly active users (MAUs), referral traffic growth, and page views (e.g., "5 million monthly active users," "651.7 million page views").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure reach and engagement with standard KPIs (MAUs, referral traffic, pageviews, growth rates) to evaluate product traction and inform marketing and editorial strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency as an improvement, not a panacea
rubrics_metrics.description: Hamamoto: "transparency is an improvement, not a panacea. 'Showing all sides [of the political spectrum] does not make the perfect solution... better than just showing one side.'"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use transparency (e.g., labeling, showing multiple sides) to improve trust and awareness, while acknowledging its limits in changing selective exposure or deep political polarization.
